source: Watermelon (ដំណាំ ឪឡឹក) cultivation factsheet, undated; source publisher not stated on the visible pages but the structure and layout are consistent with MAFF/GDA vegetable-crop factsheet series (elibrary.maff.gov.kh). Uploaded PDF, no cover page present.
text:
Watermelon is a fruit-type crop harvested when it reaches full maturity, since unlike some fruits it does not continue to ripen well after picking. Farmers are advised to check both ends of the fruit: when the tendril nearest the fruit stem has dried and turned brown/withered, and when tapping the fruit produces a dull, heavy-sounding thud rather than a sharp or hollow sound, the fruit is generally ready to harvest. Fruit should be cut with a knife or pruning shears rather than pulled, leaving a short piece of stem attached, and then transported carefully to storage or market to avoid bruising.

Depending on variety, common yield-type watermelons mature roughly 55-60 days after sowing for early varieties, with medium varieties around 65-75 days and later varieties around 80-90 days after sowing, and are typically ready for a full harvest around 90-95 days to about 100-107 days after sowing depending on variety and conditions.

Expected yield performance mentioned in this source is around 34-40 tons per hectare for good crop management, though the source also references watermelon yield figures on the order of 15-20 tons per hectare in some management scenarios, and separately mentions yields of roughly 45-50 tons per hectare for red-fleshed dessert varieties under good management (figures vary by variety and management level, so should be read as indicative ranges rather than a single fixed number).

For marketing, harvest timing is generally planned around expected market demand, and farmers are advised to avoid harvesting all fruit at once where possible, staggering harvest to spread supply and reduce the risk of price drops from an oversupplied local market at any one time.
